original_question: How does changing the topology of connections in a computer network influence the quality of network performance when the network is modeled by geodetic graphs, especially in terms of systemic hierarchy, diameter, vertex connectivity, reliability, cost, flexibility of topological change, and the number of graphs of a given diameter that represent the same network topology?
target_in_paper: Description of the Open Problems, Section C ("Open Problems Related to Computer Networks"), specifically the unlabeled open problem: "An open problem is to research how the change of topology of connections influences the quality of network performance." The immediately preceding Section C context says this comparison is relevant in the homeomorphic case, where one studies graphs of a fixed diameter d representing the same network topology. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
correct_elements: The draft correctly targets the paper's computer-network application setting, keeps geodetic graphs at the center, focuses on network-performance quality, and includes the very quality indices named in Section C: systemic hierarchy, diameter, vertex connectivity, reliability, cost, and flexibility of topological change. It also reflects the nearby Section C remark that, in the homeomorphic case, one wants the exact count of graphs of a given diameter d that represent the same network topology. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
missing_details: The draft does not identify that the official source is an unlabeled open problem in Section C, rather than a theorem, proposition, or enumeration formula. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

It omits the local graph-theoretic definitions used to make the question stand alone: a geodetic graph has a unique geodesic between every pair of distinct vertices; d(G) is the greatest distance between two vertices; homeomorphic graphs are obtained by inserting vertices on edges; and vertex connectivity is the minimum number of vertices whose deletion disconnects the graph. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

It does not make explicit that the paper discusses topology change specifically "in the case of homeomorphism," so the intended comparison is among homeomorphic geodetic graphs of fixed diameter d that represent the same network topology. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

It blends the main Section C open problem with neighboring motivation about counting graphs of diameter d; in the paper, that count is contextual support for studying topology change, not the official wording of the open problem itself. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

It does not note that Section C also states a separate, neighboring open problem: to find a single model and an adequate optimization technique capable of handling many network-quality characteristics simultaneously. That is related, but distinct from the topology-change question. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

The note itself does not formalize systemic hierarchy, reliability, cost, or flexibility of topological change into explicit objective functions; if one wanted a fully formal optimization problem, those definitions would have to be imported from the cited network-design references rather than from this note. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

Ambient ring/field, operator definitions from algebra, homogeneity, polynomial degree restrictions, nilpotency conditions, and quantifiers such as "for all sufficiently large m" are not part of this paper's setup; the relevant mathematical objects here are graphs G and their diameter d. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
refined_question: For a computer network modeled by a geodetic graph G (that is, a graph in which every pair of distinct vertices is joined by a unique geodesic), and specifically among homeomorphic geodetic graphs of a fixed diameter d that represent the same network topology, how does changing the topology of connections affect the network's operational-quality indices named in the paper—systemic hierarchy, diameter, vertex connectivity, reliability, cost, and flexibility of topological change? ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
justification: The draft most naturally matches Section C because it reproduces the paper's distinctive network-performance vocabulary and its adjoining discussion of homeomorphic realizations of the same topology at a fixed diameter d. The nearest official formulation is therefore the Section C open problem on how changes in connection topology affect network performance, not the Section B enumeration questions or the Section D rewriting-systems problem. To make the question stand alone without broadening it, the rewrite imports only the definitions placed immediately before Section C: geodetic graph, diameter, homeomorphism, and vertex connectivity. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
